So the pool really is pb_window.c's own compiler-generated block, `@37`/`@109` are MWCC's local pool labels for it, and the name difference is a genuine NonMatching-TU artifact and NOT a btricol-class wrong-symbol defect. The law's broader TU-wide screen (grep every extern whose name is neither in symbols.txt nor defined in the tree) was also run and found ONE hit, `gUpVector`, which is DECLARED BUT NEVER REFERENCED and therefore emits no relocation; it was removed in its own byte-identical commit as flip hygiene. claim.law.rebase-add-operand-order-follows-source-expression.20260831.v1 APPLIED and its diagnostic is the second substantive result: regnorm --map flags five INCONSISTENT FPR entries (f0 -> f0x18/f1x10/f2x3, f1 -> f0x12/f1x4/f5x4/f2x3, f2 -> f1x4/f3x3/f0x3/f4x2/f2x1, f3 -> f2x3/f1x2/f4x2, f4 -> f4x4/f1x2), which is the law's stated tell for commuted source operands, so the RENAMING rows were read individually as the law directs. THE TELL IS NEGATIVE HERE: every apparently-transposed row is value-identical once the operand REGISTERS are resolved. At @0x00a8 target `fsubs f0,f0,f1` vs ours `fsubs f0,f1,f0` looks commuted, but @0x0090/@0x0094 establish target f0=the 0.0f pool constant and f1=the field at 116(r3) while ours holds the opposite binding, so both compute field-minus-constant. The same resolution holds at @0x00c8, @0x049c-@0x04a4 (target f3=224(r1), f2=220(r1); ours the reverse), @0x04b8-@0x04bc and @0x0608-@0x061c. THE SCREEN CONFIRMS v1 RATHER THAN REFUTING IT, which is the point worth recording: regnorm reports 655 paired, 52 renaming, ZERO STRUCTURAL, 8 unpaired -> COUNT-MISMATCH. Zero STRUCTURAL rows means v1's SCHEDULE label is HONEST, in direct contrast to the sibling pbWinSetup park in the same TU whose REGISTER_ONLY label the same screen refuted. Per claim.park-law-age-revisit-census.20260831.v1 a REGISTER_ONLY label in this corpus is right less than half the time; this record is a datapoint that a SCHEDULE label carrying a real mechanism can survive the screen intact, so the census's scepticism should not be read as blanket distrust of every inherited label. ONE REFINEMENT TO v1's FORENSICS: v1 states 'the ENTIRE residual is one instruction: the shared 0.0f pool load'. regnorm's 8 unpaired lines resolve to TWO such sites, not one - T@0x0078 `lfs f1,0(0)` against O@0x0038 `lfs f2,0(0)`, and T@0x0430 `lfs f0,0(0)` against O@0x042c `lfs f1,0(0)` (each load plus its EMB_SDA21 reloc line accounts for 2 of the 8). Both are first-loads of a repeatedly-used pool literal placed one stall-slot differently and coloured one FPR differently, so the MECHANISM v1 named is correct and unchanged; the count is two instances of it rather than one. Everything else regnorm sees is the downstream FPR recolour, 52 rows of pure renaming at identical offsets.
